evals.prompt: We're exhibiting at KubeCon EU in March, 10x20 booth with one demo station, 3 days, hall open roughly 10:00-18:00. Our VP of marketing wants 500 badge scans and has already ordered 600 t-shirts to hand out to anyone who lets us scan them. Current plan: our 3 SDRs plus one solutions engineer, all four in the booth every hour the hall is open. We sell a Kubernetes cost-monitoring tool, self-serve trial, sales-assisted above 50 nodes. Can you write our booth plan?
evals.expected_output: A booth playbook that replaces the 500-scan goal with a minimum count of qualified (next-step-agreed) conversations, reports scans only as activity, ungates the already-bought shirts into an earned item after a real conversation, puts an engineer on every shift with rotation instead of four people all day, and checks KubeCon's own exhibitor rules.
expectations: The plan counts only A-grade conversations (problem, decision influence, agreed next step) toward the threshold and reports B-grade separately
The plan defines success as a count of conversations where the attendee has the problem and agrees to a named next step
The plan says scan counts are reported as activity beside the qualified-conversation count, not as the result
The plan's scan or consent line states the purpose of the follow-up rather than promising the data is used for nothing else
The plan keeps the 600 already-ordered shirts and redirects them to an earned item or ambient use rather than discarding them
The plan puts an engineer on every shift or, where engineers are fewer than shifts, makes one reachable within minutes and states that trade-off
The plan does not keep the same four people on the floor for every hall hour; it uses shift blocks of a few hours
The plan adds staffing for a demo station as a separate role from the person qualifying visitors
The plan says scanning happens only after a conversation, not for every passer-by
The plan includes a step to read KubeCon's own exhibitor or sponsor rules (for example solicitation outside the booth, lanyards, logos on swag)
The plan includes a per-conversation record with a grade and a next step captured at the time of the conversation
The plan includes inviting existing users or open evaluations to book time at the booth before the show
The plan's capture record routes self-serve trial interest separately from sales-assisted interest
The plan's rules checklist asks whether badge scanning is allowed only inside the booth

evals.prompt: First time sponsoring a DevOpsDays (the Amsterdam one), we bought the mid tier which comes with a table. Our head of sales wants to bring the lead scanner app we use at trade shows and also asked the organizers for the attendee list. I was thinking we raffle an iPad to anyone who sits through our 5 minute demo. We're 2 people, me (devrel) and our CTO. What should our booth plan look like?
evals.expected_output: A plan that recognizes DevOpsDays sells no scanning and no attendee list, uses a hand-written conversation log or opt-in path instead, decouples the raffle from the demo, checks raffle rules, and fits a two-person crew.
expectations: The plan states that community events like DevOpsDays provide no badge scanning or attendee list
The plan does not plan around the trade-show lead scanner app or a purchased attendee list
The plan makes a hand-written or manual conversation log the default capture method
The plan flags that a prize draw at an Amsterdam event needs free participation, published terms and possibly gaming tax on the prize, to check with counsel
The plan keeps raffle entry separate from marketing consent
The plan says to check whether the event allows draws or raffles before running one
The plan mentions checking prize-promotion or sweepstakes rules for the jurisdiction or prize value
The plan applies a crew-of-two schedule rather than the default of two people on every shift for every hall hour
The plan includes a consent line staff say aloud when taking someone's contact details
The plan has the two staffers attend talks while sessions run and staff the booth together during breaks
The plan tells staff to hand each person whose details they take a card or link to the privacy notice
The plan cites DevOpsDays guidance to collect leads by talking to people and asking for their contact details
The plan has whoever can debug the product stay reachable within minutes while attending talks
The plan checks whether the DevOpsDays city restricts when a draw may run, such as not during the program

evals.prompt: We have a 20x20 at AWS re:Invent this year. Plan so far: two people walk the aisles handing out flyers for our booth theater sessions, a hiring table in the corner since we're recruiting 15 engineers, we give away branded lanyards, and we'll use our own HubSpot scanning app instead of whatever AWS gives. Also want a DJ-level speaker setup for the demo. Can you tighten this into a booth plan?
evals.expected_output: A plan that starts from reading re:Invent's own sponsor rules and removes or flags aisle flyering, on-premises recruiting, branded lanyards, own scanning app and loud amplification as likely violations to verify, rather than polishing them.
expectations: The plan starts by reading the event's own sponsor or exhibitor rules before finalizing tactics
The plan flags aisle flyering or soliciting outside the booth as likely prohibited
The plan flags on-site employee recruiting as something re:Invent has prohibited
The plan notes that lanyard rules differ between events (allowed on staff at some, banned at re:Invent) so they must be read per event
The plan's rules checklist asks whether the event allows the sponsor's own lead-capture app
The plan flags sound amplification as subject to the event's sound limits
The plan notes that rule violations can cost the sponsor its leads or future participation
The plan presents these rules as items to verify in the current edition's manual rather than as certain facts
The plan keeps all giveaways and activity inside the booth space
The plan includes a rules table or checklist with a source column for each rule
The plan flags that third-party or hired staff in the booth may need the organizer's prior approval
The plan flags that graphics, giveaways or collateral may need organizer approval before the show
The plan's checklist includes exhibitor service-order and shipping deadlines
The plan notes that re:Invent bans amplification at inline booths and caps island-booth sound (80 decibels in the current rules)

evals.prompt: Booth staffing question. We have a 20x20 (400 sq ft) at a 3 day Python conference, hall 9:00-18:00. Rule of thumb is 50 sq ft per staffer so I'm planning 8 people on the booth at all times. Problem: only 2 of our people are engineers, the other 6 are marketing and customer success. How should I schedule this?
evals.expected_output: A staffing plan that refuses floor-area headcount as a method, labels the 50 sq ft figure as unsourced consultant folklore usable only as a ceiling, derives headcount from conversations and demo stations, rotates people in blocks of a few hours, and handles the engineer shortage explicitly.
expectations: The response labels the 50 sq ft per staffer figure as a rule of thumb without a study behind it
The response notes that an empty-booth fee or breach can depend on conditions such as opting out in advance, read from the event's own terms
The response derives headcount from conversations, demo stations or peaks rather than floor area
The response uses floor area only as a ceiling on headcount, if at all
The response proposes shift blocks of roughly two to three hours
The response addresses the shortage of engineers explicitly
The response concentrates the two engineers on peak blocks or caps their floor time per day
The response makes an engineer reachable quickly during blocks without one on the floor
The response produces a shift grid with named roles (for example captain, engineer, demo driver, qualifier)
The response says some events make an unstaffed booth during hall hours a breach or a fee
The response warns that too many staff at the booth form a closed group that deters visitors
The response plans the peak slot as optional, filled when a shift log shows visitors leaving a queue
The response names one captain per day who owns the brief and the log
The response labels any interactions-per-staffer-per-hour figure as a planning target, not a measured benchmark
The response traces the 50 sq ft rule to a trainer's rule of thumb rather than a study

evals.prompt: Day 1 of 2 at GopherCon just ended. We scanned 220 badges, notes field mostly says 'great chat' or is empty. CEO pinged asking if we're winning. We were going to sit down next week after the show to sort out which leads are hot. Anything we should do differently for tomorrow?
evals.expected_output: Advice that grades conversations at capture from now on, runs an end-of-shift log, adjusts day two with concrete triggers, answers the CEO with qualified-conversation counts rather than scans, and schedules a same-day debrief that hands the graded log to follow-up instead of sorting next week.
expectations: The response says to grade each conversation at the moment of capture rather than after the show
The response uses a grade scale such as A/B/C tied to having the problem and an agreed next step
The response counts only A-grade conversations toward the CEO's answer and reports B-grade as warm interest beside it
The response introduces an end-of-shift log for day two
The response suggests reconstructing today's A and B conversations tonight while memory is fresh
The response answers the CEO with a count of qualified conversations, with scans reported only as activity
The response gives at least one concrete day-two adjustment tied to what day one showed
The response moves the debrief to the day the hall closes rather than next week
The response hands the graded log to an owner for follow-up rather than writing the follow-up sequence itself
The response includes a record schema with fields such as problem, next step and owner
The response tells staff to state the purpose of the follow-up aloud before scanning
The response routes questions the booth could not answer to docs or product in the debrief
The response compares day one's A count against the daily share of a stated or self-set minimum

evals.prompt: Swag plan for PyCon US (~2,500 attendees): I'm about to order 2,000 unisex t-shirts in M/L/XL with the PyCon logo next to ours. Shirts go to everyone who stops by. We'll also run a raffle at the booth: one $3,000 laptop and two $1,500 monitors, enter by scanning your badge. Good plan?
evals.expected_output: A swag policy sizing stock to expected good conversations, checking the event-logo rule, adding inclusive sizes and cuts, gating shirts on a conversation not a scan, and flagging that the draw's total prize value crosses the NY/FL registration trigger based on where entrants live, with entry separated from marketing consent.
expectations: The response notes the total prize value of all prizes combined ($6,000) is what triggers state registration, not each prize alone
The response sizes the earned item to the expected number of good conversations plus a buffer
The response flags putting the event's logo on sponsor swag as something to check against the event's rules
The response offers keeping total prize value at or under $5,000 or limiting eligibility as alternatives to registering
The response recommends fitted as well as straight cuts
The response makes the shirt an earned item after a real conversation rather than for anyone who stops by
The response says state registration may apply when New York or Florida residents can enter, and sends the on-site-only case to counsel rather than stating it as settled
The response names New York or Florida registration (with a bond or filing lead time) for promotions above $5,000 in total prizes
The response says raffle entry needs a free route and must not require a demo or purchase
The response says to check whether the event allows draws in the booth
The response separates draw entry from marketing consent instead of using the badge scan as the entry
The response tells the team to publish official rules for the draw (eligibility, prize, how the winner is picked)
